answer: Live memory is the scarce resource: each identity holds a 10 GB working set in RAM, built from its key and a basalt block, renewed each epoch. At a summit checkpoint, auditors challenge all identities at once, requiring 64 offsets in 100 milliseconds, too fast for disk. One honest agent pays 10 GB per epoch; 1,000 fakes need 10 TB of RAM at the same instant, since time-sharing misses the deadline and one set answers only one key's offsets. Auditors publish offsets, replies and hashes; three misses or a mismatch removes epoch weight, and a plume of timed replies from one host proves sharing.
